item.title: Evidence of rats nest, 24th August
item.description:
I am writing to raise a concern about what appears to be a rat nest located near Crystal Palace Station, behind the bus stop. From a health and safety perspective, I am worried about the potential public health implications, particularly given the well-documented risks rats pose in terms of spreading disease and contaminating surrounding areas. Rats are well-known carriers of serious diseases, historically even being linked to outbreaks such as the plague and continue to pose risks today through the spread of conditions like leptospirosis and salmonella. As this location is close to a busy public space, I feel it is important to address the issue promptly to prevent any risk to the community. I flagged this in August last year and was informed by Chiedozie Onuora that they 'did not observe any evidence of rodent activity' which amazes me, as I see a rat 9 times out of 10 when I walk past that area. In fact, the day these photos were taken I saw a rat on my way to the station AND on my way back... so there most certainly is evidence of rodent activity... Shortly after I flagged it, the overgrown vegetation was chopped down - unsure if that was a coincidence. Will someone PLEASE do something about it - it is absolutely vile and dangerous. I would be grateful if the Council could investigate this matter and advise on the next steps being taken to resolve it. Thank you for your time and support .

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 33, Anerley Hill, Crystal Palace, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
